# Independent audit: joint projective-energy concavity and equality

Audited the complete source
`candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56`,
Sections 1--7. **PASS; no repair identified.** This is a proof audit,
not a numerical confirmation. It concerns ordinary full-dimensional
convex bodies with marked interior points, and supplies no mixed-integer
center selection or OC conclusion.

After the proof audit, the source's exact calibration verifier was also
rerun: **1,639 exact checks PASS**. Those checks are supplementary and
are not used in place of the general conditional-substitution argument.

## 1. Attainment and escort normalization

The inner ball makes the admissible parameter set bounded; compactness
of the body makes it open and gives a positive denominator bound on
every compact parameter neighborhood. The Hessian in (3) is strictly
positive in every nonzero direction because a full-dimensional convex
body is not supported on the corresponding hyperplane.

At a boundary parameter, its zero-denominator contact point is separated
from the hyperplane through the origin perpendicular to that parameter.
The fixed cone over an inner disk consequently has positive Jacobian
constant times `t^(d-1)`. On `delta_k<=t<=2delta_k`, the denominator is
at most a fixed multiple of `delta_k`; integrating gives the claimed
lower bound proportional to `1/delta_k`. The contact denominator is
positive before the limit. This also works in dimension one with the
zero-dimensional disk interpreted as its single point. Thus the unique
minimizer is attained strictly inside the admissible set.

Dotting stationarity with the minimizer, and using `L=1+a.(x-y)`, gives
`int L^(-d-2)=int L^(-d-1)=E` with the printed exponents and signs.
The escort density therefore has mass one, barycenter `y`, and expected
denominator one. Its positivity and neighborhood extension follow from
the strictly positive denominator on compact `K`.

## 2. Conditional substitution for arbitrary convex supports

The slice-continuity argument is valid without a smooth boundary. If a
point in the relative interior of a full-dimensional slice over an
interior projected prefix lay on the body's boundary, a supporting
normal would vanish in every remaining slice direction. It would then
support the projection at an interior point, a contradiction. Outside
the limiting closed slice, membership is eventually false by compactness.
The remaining slice boundary has measure zero. Dominated convergence in
a fixed box proves marginal continuity; interior slices supply strict
positivity.

The next-coordinate projection intervals have continuous endpoints on
the interior prefix domain. Positive continuous conditional densities
give strictly increasing cumulative distributions and locally continuously
differentiable inverse quantiles in their current coordinates. Joint
continuity follows by bracketing each inverse value between two interior
test values. The diagonal derivative formula telescopes exactly to
`1/rho(X)`.

The weighted sum map is triangular and strictly increasing in each
current coordinate. Its recursively described image intervals vary
continuously, giving an open image and a continuous recursive inverse.
Successive one-dimensional substitutions, starting with the last
coordinate, prove (8) for nonnegative Borel integrands. This requires
neither unproved derivatives in earlier coordinates nor an area formula
for a globally smooth map. The generalized Holder step (9) has the
correct direction and includes its weights exactly once.

## 3. Joint concavity and the entropy form

For the escort maps, the diagonal products are
`E_i L_i(X_i)^(d+2)`. Determinant Holder followed by scalar power-mean
convexity gives exactly `J_S>=A^d Lbar^(d+2)`. The weights defining
`Lbar` sum to one, and its cube mean is one. The combined target
denominator is positive and also has cube mean one because the sum map
has the required marked barycenter. Positivity on each separately
displaced input is not needed and is not assumed.

The image lies in the actual Minkowski sum. Substitution and the final
Holder inequality therefore bound the integral for EVERY admissible
target parameter below by `A^d`. Taking its infimum preserves this lower
bound. This verifies the joint result in every `d>=1`.

The monotonicity argument respects the different admissible parameter
domains. Affine scaling, the convex domain of fiber-interior marked
points, and the resulting joint fiberwise concavity follow as stated.
At the ordinary centroid, zero is the unique minimizer; conversely an
energy equal to ordinary volume makes zero a minimizer and recovers the
centroid. No statement about a lattice-preserving projective map is used.

In the entropy representation, the exponent is `(d+1)/(d+2)`.
Holder applied to `(rho L)^p L^(-p)` gives the printed upper bound since
the affine moment constraint gives `int rho L=1`. The escort density
attains it: its `p`-moment is `E^(1/(d+2))`. There is no unmentioned
pointwise upper bound on admissible densities.

## 4. Complete equality classification

Use the attained target minimizer in the full chain of inequalities.
Equality in the final theorem forces each nonnegative intermediate
integral difference to vanish. Strict scalar power convexity gives
`L_i(X_i)=L_j(X_j)` almost everywhere. Equality in determinant Holder
gives proportional positive diagonal derivative vectors. Taking their
products identifies the proportionality constant as
`(E_i/E_j)^(1/d)`. For `d=1`, the same derivative ratio follows directly
from the diagonal product formula and the equality of denominators.

It would not suffice to infer full homothety from a single triangular
frame. The source correctly repeats the proof in every orthonormal
frame with arbitrary first direction `e`. The first-coordinate
quantiles then have a constant derivative ratio almost everywhere;
their local continuous differentiability makes their difference an
affine constant throughout the open interval. The escort barycenters
determine that constant, and full interior support identifies their
endpoint limits with the body's projection endpoints. Thus all centered
support functions have the same positive scale, proving marked positive
homothety. Conversely such marked homotheties attain equality by affine
scaling.

For two distinct marked points in one fixed bounded body, homothety
would have scale one by volume and would require a nonzero translational
symmetry. Hence the fixed-body energy to the power `1/d` is strictly
concave. This proof covers nonsmooth bodies and dimension one; it asserts
no quantitative modulus and no arithmetic consequence.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
